workshop.what: Open with the film, then today’s heat in your city
workshop.why: A shared picture before any discussion.

workshop.what: A week in the heat, in small groups, one worker each
workshop.why: People feel where protection fails, before they debate it.

workshop.what: Groups report: what reached their worker, and what broke
workshop.why: Turns individual stories into a shared list of gaps.

workshop.what: Plan a response together, on one screen
workshop.why: Owners, money and triggers for the gaps the groups found. Run the stress test if time allows.

workshop.what: Agree the next three decisions, and who takes each
workshop.why: Leave with commitments, recorded on the plan’s status ladder.

workshopTips: One person drives the screen; everyone else talks.
Use a real place the room knows, but keep the worker composite.
Record what is agreed, and what is only discussed. The plan’s status ladder does this.
Close by printing the plan, or copying it into the meeting notes.

workshopCommunity.what: Share what the hot weeks were like here last year
workshopCommunity.why: Start from what people know. Talk about places and conditions, not about who is to blame.

workshopCommunity.what: Follow one worker’s week in the heat, together on one screen
workshopCommunity.why: A shared story makes it easier to talk about our own. The worker is made up, so no one has to share theirs.

workshopCommunity.what: Find actions for the places we live and work
workshopCommunity.why: Workplaces, homes, markets and streets: pick what we can start ourselves this season.

workshopCommunity.what: See who needs to say yes, and what each would need
workshopCommunity.why: Some protection needs partners: an employer, a landlord, a market committee, a clinic or the local council.

workshopCommunity.what: Agree what we will do, and what we will ask of whom
workshopCommunity.why: A name next to each action, and each request written as an invitation to work together.

workshopCommunityTips: Use the languages people speak, and read the screen aloud.
Keep the worker made up. Never share someone’s own story without their permission.
Talk about conditions and solutions, not blame.
Note what the group can do on its own, and what needs a partner.
If anyone feels unwell from the heat, stop and look after them first.
Close by reading the list back, then print or photograph it.
workshopCommunityBefore: Choose a cool, shaded place, with drinking water for everyone.
Pick a time that does not cost people a day’s work.
Open the worker exercise, practical actions and the coordinator’s simulation in three tabs. No screen? Print the action cards.
Ask who will write down what is agreed.
